spans.title: The Letter at Ten O'Clock
spans.blurb: A letter of sad tidings arrives at ten o'clock. A woman who dare not be seen in daylight kisses the corner bed goodbye and slips into the night.

spans.title: The Scuffle Next Door
spans.blurb: Two boys leaning out a night window hear a policeman seize a prowler next door, and the whole household tumbles downstairs into a small, delicious mystery.

books.pairNote: Separate scenes with different characters; no shared text or shared payoff.

spans.title: The Body in Millfield Lane
spans.blurb: Walking home past midnight in the rain, a very new doctor finds a dead man lying across a lonely lane and goes to fetch the police.

spans.title: Hoofs, Hoofs, Hoofs
spans.blurb: A wounded Mountie and the killer holding his gun sit marooned on one boulder while a caribou migration thunders past, trading taunts to keep from going mad.
spans.brokenNote: The text stops mid-sentence ('filled with clashing antlers and the'), so the standoff simply cuts off with no ending.

spans.title: Too Much Fish
spans.blurb: A young hunter comes ashore with more fish than one man can eat, and the chief's sharp-tongued daughter stops by, carrying a message that could mean combat.

spans.title: The Silver Egg
spans.blurb: Against every instinct, a stone-age hunter walks east past sabre-tooth country, drawn by an urge he cannot fight toward a silver egg taller than the trees.
spans.spoilerNote: Reveals what the silver ovoid is and the visitors' ecology experiment, the premise the full story builds its opening mystery around.

books.pairNote: Village courtship and the alien summons are separate beats with no shared payoff.

spans.title: Hello, Barton
spans.blurb: In an empty town, every phone rings for one old man. The voice on the line is young, tireless, and impossible to hang up on.
spans.spoilerNote: Reveals that the caller is Barton's own younger recorded self, the central conceit the full story unfolds gradually.

spans.title: I See Her Night and Day
spans.blurb: A year on, Jack is a wasted shadow of himself, flinching from something no one else can see. His friend gently coaxes out what happened.

spans.title: The Mesmerist's Betrothed
spans.blurb: A parlour mesmerist makes a boy play Mozart he never learned, and his betrothed begs to be put under too. He tells what came of giving in.

books.pairNote: The short's closing shock, 'I killed her,' is the very event the story span recounts in full, so reading either first flattens the other.

spans.title: The Eminent Ex-Congressman
spans.blurb: Peter Q. Hornswoggle, eminent ex-congressman, holds a barroom audience spellbound with tales of apple-parers and applause, until a newspaper item lights a gleam in his eye.

spans.title: A Very Popular Safe
spans.blurb: A chemist wakes to crashing glassware and finds two rival burglars brawling in his laboratory. Then a third walks in, and this one handles a revolver expertly.

books.pairNote: The bar sketch introduces the schemer whom the burglary scene later catches red-handed; complementary, not duplicated.

spans.title: Porky's Confession
spans.blurb: Cheerful Porky Jenks arrives rumpled and haunted, begging his writer friend to believe the impossible: last week, sitting by his window, he became somebody else entirely.

spans.title: Aunt Lona's Inspection
spans.blurb: A young man enters his own house hat in hand and is met by a crochet-wielding aunt with the bearing of a drill sergeant.

spans.title: Frozen to the Pane
spans.blurb: Someone has peeped through the window on two nights running. On his way past the frosted pane, Renfro finds what the cold kept for him.
